Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and inherited rollout evidence, then inspect both moving-window wake views before proposing the single candidate. I’ll also consult the fish-control bookshelf per the required transfer protocol and keep the candidate rationale separate from the reusable guidance.

I’m using two workspace skills here: `read-wake-visual-signals-first` to make the visual diagnosis from both required views, and `fish-control-primitives` to constrain any mechanism transfer to normalized body-frame feedback. I’ll apply their instructions before touching the policy.

The scalar evidence separates three behaviors: the prefilled seed makes substantial progress then reverses, the strongest sampled candidate reaches a `1.135L` near miss before diverging, and another finite candidate barely improves before exiting. I’m now checking whether those distinctions are visible in both wake views and consistent with the detailed state/action diagnostics.

The visual/metric cross-check supports one focused extension of the best sampled mechanism: retain its geometry-gated mean-curvature redirect and add a continuous terminal approach hold. The near miss remains self-propelled with a coherent wake, but reaches `1.135L` at about `0.643U` while the head command is clipped and the first joint is near its angle limit; the turn completes only after the fish has passed below the target. I’m recording that diagnosis and the bookshelf transfer before editing the candidate.

The policy now differs from the strongest sampled redirect only inside the near-and-closing regime: far-field propulsion and target geometry mapping are unchanged, while terminal cadence and joint-rate energy are reduced smoothly and released on recession. I’m now promoting the cross-candidate evidence—not the unevaluated new candidate—into the durable guidance.
The candidate and durable lesson are both updated. I’m invoking the workspace’s required check runner now; it will validate the policy contract and guidance delta without running CFD.

The configured check-runner model is unavailable in this environment, so the delegated invocation could not start. I’ve read its exact three-command contract and am running those checks directly, separately, with the same no-CFD constraint.

The first check found a rendered-workspace metadata defect: `README.md` marks the same guidance parent as copied twice, so the checker cannot resolve a unique assigned parent. I’m removing only that duplicate manifest entry, then rerunning the required check; this does not alter the experiment or solver surface.

All three prescribed checks now pass: the guidance/notes semantic-delta check, the Julia policy contract and finite-action check, and the editable-boundary check. I’m doing one final audit of the exact workspace deltas and candidate uniqueness; no CFD will be run here.

Completed exactly one Phase 2 candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1) preserves the evidenced geometry-gated redirect and adds a normalized near-and-closing approach hold with cadence relief and joint-rate damping.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) contains the visual diagnosis, hypothesis, falsification criteria, and bookshelf transfer block.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:57) now records the reusable cross-candidate redirect and terminal-capture lesson.

All prescribed checks passed: guidance semantic delta, Julia policy contract, parameter-schema completeness, finite bounded actions, far-field behavior preservation, and editable boundary. The configured check-runner model was unavailable, so its exact commands were run directly. No CFD was run.
